title: Film portrayals of musicians: Ben Vereen, Teddy Buckner and Duke
summary: Edison and Dance discuss who played Armstrong, why Teddy Buckner should have done it, and who might portray Ellington.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: Oh, Cicely Tyson.
Cicely Tyson. She's -- oh, she's fantastic. She's a superb actress, you know. And Ben Vereen is all right, but he portrayed Louie Armstrong.
Yeah, I saw that on TV.
Yeah.
Well, it was fair.

Why didn't they get a trumpet player? Teddy Buckner, He loved Louie Armstrong all his life. He looks like Louie and he's been playing like him all his life. They get somebody -- Ben Vereen is all right. To do what he does, he's fantastic in what he does.
Who played the trumpet in that film?

I don't know. They should have gotten Teddy Buckner, because he's been a Louie Armstrong idol -- oh, he's been a disciple of Pops' for years, and he's still -- he sounds just like Louie Armstrong. Today, he does. To Disneyworld -- Disneyland, he's got a band out there. He's had one for years. He sounds just like Pops. Still does. And I think it would have been much -- I would -- well, maybe that's the reason why I'm not a producer, because I would have gotten Teddy Buckner to do that.
Well, I mean, this seems to be -- you know, every -- it's not only black either, because you know, you take the film they made on Benny Goodman. They hammed that up and made that ridiculous.
Well, the Glenn Miller Story was good with James Stewart. That was good.
Yeah, I suppose so. I never saw that, but I've heard it was.
Yeah, that was good. But to do a life story -- I wonder who they're going to get when they really do
a life story of Pops. That was just an hour TV show.
Yeah, just an episode out of his life, wasn't it?
Yeah.
Well, who do you think they'll get to do Duke?
(Laughter.)
Get somebody ridiculous, I'm sure.
Yeah, they'll get somebody that they're just trying to make a star, to promote him, you know, which will be really -- it's comical when they get somebody like that to portray --

It's okay if they do it -- like if they were doing it 50 years later, it's not too bad, because then the people don't know. But it's when they do it soon after, when all the people are around who knew this man, just like they knew Pops, you know, and it's difficult to accept.
Yeah, it is, it is.
